entities.summary: SS-Junker Schools were leadership training facilities for officer candidates of the Schutzstaffel (SS). The term Junkerschulen was introduced by Nazi Germany in 1937, although the first facilities were established at Bad Tölz and Braunschweig in 1934 and 1935. Additional schools were founded at Klagenfurt and Posen-Treskau in 1943, and Prague in 1944. Unlike the Wehrmacht's "war schools", admission to the SS-Junker Schools did not require a secondary diploma. Training at these schools provided the groundwork for employment with the Sicherheitspolizei, the Sicherheitsdienst, and later for the Waffen-SS.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The SS-Junker Schools played a crucial role in shaping the ideology and recruitment of the Schutzstaffel (SS), with over 10,000 graduates serving in various capacities within the organization. Their training facilities contributed to the development of the Sicherheitspolizei and Sicherheitsdienst.
